mechanism_narrative: A positive monthly change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) relative to the prior month signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and equity risk premiums, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically causes immediate equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% in a single month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in the last month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals deteriorating economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220 and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 600,000 units signals weak consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST < 600, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 (2017=100) signals a significant supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to increased cost pressures and reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A positive monthly change in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the prior month signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST rises month-over-month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening cycle (defined by UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly), a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly and UNRATE falls, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is < 0.03.
